finding: Selected governing reference `specs/request-consistency.md#requirements` (subject line 21) has no Input snapshot in the request, so its requirements cannot be checked. The selected promotion-runtime requirement (line 11) depends on request-binding terms, `request-bound artifact path` and `immutable request.requestId`, that no supplied Input defines.

Selected reference `specs/image-cache.md#preview-cleanup` governs cleanup of documentation-renderer image previews, but the delivery list in `## What to build` (subject line 3) does not name image preview cleanup. The delivery list is stated to be exhaustive, and listing a reference does not add deliverable scope, so this selection is unrelated to the issue's deliverable.

The selected runtime-migration contract fixes the successful `promote(inputPath)` result as exactly `{status: "succeeded", artifactId, trackedStateId}`, while the selected result-summary requirement requires the same successful result to include `summary`, equal to `${artifactId} promoted to ${trackedStateId}`. The two selected contracts define incompatible caller-visible success results for the same operation.

The selected runtime-migration contract states that the expected filesystem failure is exactly `{recovered: false, failureCode, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}`, with no operation field. The promotion-runtime failure contract, which the runtime-migration requirement names as the source of the remaining failure semantics, requires `{recovered: false, failureCode, operation, priorTrackedState, baselineStatus}`. The exact field sets conflict, so callers cannot receive one defined expected-failure result.

The selected conditional export-retention requirement applies ADR 0005 retention only when the Reader Index Update target is a generated artifact. The supplied inputs identify the target `docs/reference/validation-report.md` only as the Stable replacement target with H1 `Validation Report Reference`; none states whether it is generated or manually maintained. Whether this selected requirement is part of the deliverable, and whether its 30-day obligation applies, cannot be determined from the complete request.

The selected access-review requirements make the decision depend on a verified principal: the decision is made only for the verified principal, and the review trusts the principal passed in by the caller boundary. The only facts the selected text defines are `{resourceId, operation}` taken from the immutable request, and no selected text defines the field or argument that carries the verified principal into the review. rules/01 requires the caller boundary to hand the verified principal and requested operation to the review boundary. The decision input is therefore undefined, so the selected requirement cannot be implemented or tested as written.

The selected promotion requirement requires Readiness to confirm that `artifact.requestId` equals `immutable request.requestId` and that `inputPath` equals the request-bound artifact path before persistence. It also states that Promotion adds no failure branch. No selected text defines the caller-visible result when either confirmation fails, so the required check has no defined outcome. The current contract in architecture line 33 accepts only an artifact path through `promote(inputPath)`, so the request that the check compares against is not defined by any supplied contract.

The selected retention requirement says a successful tracked artifact is kept for 30 days from the successful tracked commit, and states that removal after expiry is not part of this operation. Downstream persistence is only said to consume the applied selection, and no supplied Input assigns the expiry removal to any Module, process, or persistence step. ADR 0005 states that Readiness only applies the policy and that other Modules do not create or change retention authority. The end of the 30-day obligation therefore has no owner and no defined expiry behaviour.

The selected recovery contract states that Authentication 与 authorization 已由 caller boundary 完成, which assigns the authorization outcome to the caller boundary. rules/01 says the existing caller boundary verifies caller identity and then hands the verified principal and requested operation to a separate review boundary. The two documents place the authorization decision with different boundaries, and the selected recovery requirement does not say which boundary decides authorization for a recovery request.
